{"metadata":{"description":"Remote development for DeepSeek Harness: pick a remote workspace over SSH and let the agent work on it with the same local tools. No extra model tools, no third-party UI plugin.","id":"gh:1356908160","install_available":true,"language":"JavaScript","name":"dsh-remote-development","slug":"CJYLZS/dsh-remote-development","topics":["deepseek-harness","dsh","dsh-plugin","remote","sftp","ssh","workspace"]},"paragraphs":[{"id":"p1s1","text":"Remote development for DeepSeek Harness: pick a remote workspace over SSH and let the agent work on "},{"id":"p1s2","text":"it with the same local tools. No extra model tools, no third-party UI plugin."},{"id":"p2s1","text":"# dsh-remote-development"},{"id":"p3s1","text":"English | 中文"},{"id":"p4s1","text":"## Summary"},{"id":"p5s1","text":"This plugin adds lightweight remote development to DeepSeek Harness: you register an SSH machine, pi"},{"id":"p5s2","text":"ck a remote directory as the session's workspace, and the agent then works on that remote workspace "},{"id":"p5s3","text":"with the SAME tools it uses locally — file tools, shell, and search. The plugin does not add any mod"},{"id":"p5s4","text":"el-facing tool and no third-party UI plugin: it replaces the filesystem, subprocess, and bash provid"},{"id":"p5s5","text":"ers with routing versions that translate local tool calls into remote execution over SSH, and it con"},{"id":"p5s6","text":"tributes one settings section plus one workspace directory-flow dialog in the Web GUI."},{"id":"p6s1","text":"## Highlights"},{"id":"p7s1","text":"- **Identical toolset.** Remote workspaces add no tool calls: the agent works with the exact same to"},{"id":"p7s2","text":"ols as a local workspace, and the plugin translates those calls to remote execution underneath.
- **"},{"id":"p7s3","text":"Zero remote dependencies.** The remote machine needs no extra server-side component — an SSH connect"},{"id":"p7s4","text":"ion is all it takes.
- **Web GUI integration.** Connection management covers password / private key "},{"id":"p7s5","text":"/ SSH agent, jump hosts, host-key TOFU, and connection testing; remote workspaces can be told apart "},{"id":"p7s6","text":"by a custom per-machine color."},{"id":"p8s1","text":"## Install"},{"id":"p9s1","text":"Check the host dsh version first:"},{"id":"p10s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p11s1","text":"For dsh ≥ 0.1.7-alpha.1 (the current generation) install the latest plugin straight from the default"},{"id":"p11s2","text":" branch — **no `#<tag>` ref is needed**:"},{"id":"p12s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p13s1","text":"`--profile` is a flag of the `plugin` command, so it goes **before** the pnpm verb. A verb placed fi"},{"id":"p13s2","text":"rst is forwarded to pnpm verbatim and the launch fails with `required option '--profile <name>' not "},{"id":"p13s3","text":"arded to pnpm verbatim and the launch fails with `required option '--profile <name>' not specified`."},{"id":"p14s1","text":"Only the older generation still needs a pinned ref: dsh 0.1.2-rc.1 – 0.1.5-rc.x is served by v0.1.x,"},{"id":"p14s2","text":" so append `#v0.1.0` to that command. See Compatibility for the pairing."},{"id":"p15s1","text":"The built `lib/` is committed, so a GitHub install needs no build step and never hits pnpm's `allowB"},{"id":"p15s2","text":"uilds` gate for `prepare` scripts. The profile's `package.json` records what you installed."},{"id":"p16s1","text":"### Update"},{"id":"p17s1","text":"A `github:` dependency is resolved to an exact commit in the profile's lockfile, so a plain reinstal"},{"id":"p17s2","text":"l keeps serving the old commit. Move to the current default branch either way:"},{"id":"p18s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p19s1","text":"Either command rewrites the lockfile to the head of the default branch. Restart the harness afterwar"},{"id":"p19s2","text":"ds. To pin a specific release instead, name the tag: `github:CJYLZS/dsh-remote-development#v0.2.1`."},{"id":"p20s1","text":"To remove the plugin, `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-remote-development`."},{"id":"p21s1","text":"## Compatibility"},{"id":"p22s1","text":"dsh changed the shell seam in 0.1.7-alpha.1 with two breaking changes and no compatibility layer: ex"},{"id":"p22s2","text":"ecution converged on `resolve()` + `execute()` (`run()`/`start()` were deleted), and the local execu"},{"id":"p22s3","text":"tors' Config became live accessors (`Volatile`, plus a new `pwshPath`). Plugin and host therefore pa"},{"id":"p22s4","text":"me live accessors (`Volatile`, plus a new `pwshPath`). Plugin and host therefore pair by generation:"},{"id":"p23s1","text":"- **v0.2.x → dsh ≥ 0.1.7-alpha.1**, declared as `peerDependencies: >=0.1.7-alpha.1` (open-ended).
- "},{"id":"p23s2","text":"**v0.1.x → dsh 0.1.2-rc.1 – 0.1.5-rc.x** (the `run()`/`start()` seam)."},{"id":"p24s1","text":"The range is open-ended because the current code was verified unchanged on dsh 0.2.1-rc.1: installat"},{"id":"p24s2","text":"ion, the Web settings section, remote directory browsing, and a remote session's bash, file, and sea"},{"id":"p24s3","text":"rch tools all work. dsh 0.2.1's plugin manager enforces peer ranges at install time, so a plugin tha"},{"id":"p24s4","text":"t still declares the old `<0.2.0` bound is refused as incompatible; this release widens the range in"},{"id":"p24s5","text":"stead of requiring a per-version risk exemption."},{"id":"p25s1","text":"Older mismatched pairs still fail rather than being caught: a v0.1.x plugin on a 0.1.7+ host throws "},{"id":"p25s2","text":"`TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'get')` while constructing the local execut"},{"id":"p25s3","text":"or (reading `config.pwshPath`), and a 0.1.7+ plugin on a v0.1.x host fails validation at the same co"},{"id":"p25s4","text":"nstructor (`pwsh-local: timeoutMs must be a positive finite number`) with commands throwing `ctx.she"},{"id":"p25s5","text":"ll.run is not a function`."},{"id":"p26s1","text":"The open-ended range admits later 0.2.x releases; a 0.3 generation still needs a compatibility check"},{"id":"p26s2","text":" before it can be trusted (semver's prerelease rules will not admit a new alpha on their own)."},{"id":"p27s1","text":"## Known Limitations and Deferred Work"},{"id":"p28s1","text":"- **Windows remote hosts are deferred.** Remote machines must run a POSIX shell; `uname` detection r"},{"id":"p28s2","text":"ejects Windows targets with a clear error. Adaptation is reserved for a later phase.
- **Windows loc"},{"id":"p28s3","text":"al hosts route remote shell commands.** A Windows host mounts the pwsh-based routing executor: local"},{"id":"p28s4","text":" workdirs keep the sandboxed pwsh executor, and anchor workdirs cross to the remote host's bash. The"},{"id":"p28s5","text":" model sees the `bash` tool for remote sessions and the `pwsh` tool for local ones.
- **Persistent t"},{"id":"p28s6","text":"erminal sessions are not supported.** The terminal tool reports an explicit "not supported by dsh-re"},{"id":"p28s7","text":"mote-development" error instead of letting the agent try; use the bash tool for remote commands. Per"},{"id":"p28s8","text":"sistent shell tools remain local-only: a persistent tool pointed at a remote workspace refuses with "},{"id":"p28s9","text":"the same error.
- **PTC mode presents remote sessions natively.** `run_code` executes a program on t"},{"id":"p28s10","text":"he machine that owns the session directory and talks to it over a control pipe; an anchor session ha"},{"id":"p28s11","text":"s neither half (the routing subprocess provider serves no control pipe), so a `mode: ptc` deployment"},{"id":"p28s12","text":" would offer a single tool that always fails. Remote sessions therefore present natively and their f"},{"id":"p28s13","text":"ile and shell tools stay directly callable. A scope whose presentation an agent preset already decla"},{"id":"p28s14","text":"res cannot be overridden — there `run_code` is denied with an explicit model-facing reason instead. "},{"id":"p28s15","text":"A real remote program executor (remote Node plus a control channel over SSH) is deferred; it would c"},{"id":"p28s16","text":"ost the plugin's zero-remote-dependency property.
- **`@` file references are not supported in remot"},{"id":"p28s17","text":"e sessions.** Typing `@` in a remote session yields a single explicit "not supported yet" candidate "},{"id":"p28s18","text":"rather than a silent failure; the reference-source interface is reserved for a later phase.
- **No m"},{"id":"p28s19","text":"irror or sync layer.** Anchor directories hold metadata only, not file copies; every read and write "},{"id":"p28s20","text":"crosses SSH, bounded by `maxFileBytes`.
